TIER 2: it changes the READ SURFACE of a live service (src/web/api/routers/diag.py), so it is not done at merge -- ict-web-api.service must be pulled and restarted before the probe that 400s today can return 200. The manager merges and drives the deploy; this lane's standing instruction is to open the PR as a draft and stop.

The APPROVAL BEING RELIED ON is already recorded, and it is the operator's, not this session's: docs/claude/work/MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json row E27 on `main` at 0e0a8f3 reads "OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-22: ADD ssh.service TO _CANONICAL_UNITS. The counts-only summariser and dropping the requirement were both offered and both declined. The privacy cost was stated in the question and accepted: sshd journal lines carry source IPs and usernames, and every session that can reach /api/diag/* will be able to read them." No R15 credential is written under docs/claude/work/approvals/ and none is claimed -- this holds for a human merge rather than self-landing on that record.
why:
E27. The /health-review skill lists `journalctl` for sshd/auth as a MANDATORY breach-sweep source (SKILL.md section "Security-breach check", source 5). _CANONICAL_UNITS is an exact-match allowlist of this project's own systemd units and has never held an ssh entry, so that source has been UNSATISFIABLE on every day since the skill was written.

MEASURED 2026-09-22 against the running web-api (https://ict-bot.duckdns.org), this session, with a positive control in the same run so a quiet result is distinguishable from a broken probe:
  CONTROL  journalctl?unit=ict-web-api.service -> HTTP 200, 3 journal lines
  unit=ssh           -> HTTP 400 {"error":"unknown_unit"}
  unit=ssh.service   -> HTTP 400 {"error":"unknown_unit"}
  unit=sshd          -> HTTP 400 {"error":"unknown_unit"}
  unit=sshd.service  -> HTTP 400 {"error":"unknown_unit"}
There was no spelling that worked; this reproduces E24's measurement independently.

THE NAME WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, and the alias is a trap worth the paragraph. On ict-bot-arm (Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS), via the vm-driver relay: `systemctl list-unit-files 'ssh*'` reports ssh.service enabled and sshd.service as an ALIAS; `systemctl show ssh.service` gives Id=ssh.service, Names="ssh.service sshd.service". systemd resolves the alias for show/is-active -- the JOURNAL MATCH DOES NOT: `journalctl -u ssh.service -n 3` returned 3 sshd lines and `journalctl -u sshd.service -n 3` returned "-- No entries --" in the same run. Allowlisting the alias would therefore have answered HTTP 200 with lines: [] and available: true (rc=0, no stderr): a breach sweep reporting CLEAN having read nothing, which is strictly worse than the 400 it replaced. `ssh.service` is the only entry added, and tests/test_web_api_diag.py now pins BOTH halves -- ssh.service accepted, sshd.service still refused 400.

SCOPE. Exactly one unit is added to _CANONICAL_UNITS. No other unit, no new route, no change to the journalctl handler, no widening of what the route can read beyond that one unit's journal.

THE DUAL-USE WAS CHECKED BEFORE PUSHING, because a read-allowlist doubling as a liveness list is how a change like this breaks something unrelated. _CANONICAL_UNITS is read at four other sites, all inside diag.py: /snapshot and /services build {unit, state} rows from it (they REPORT systemctl state, they do not assert it, and ssh.service is active on the host); _timer_units() filters to `.timer` and cannot match it. Outside diag.py the only references are COMMENTS (src/web/api/routers/health_snapshots.py:198, scripts/ops/work_digest_now.py:67, .github/workflows/system-actions.yml:46) plus scripts/check_diag_unit_allowlist.py, which AST-parses the tuple to check the other direction (every deploy/ unit is queryable) and so is unaffected -- verified by running it: 47 deploy units scanned, 41 allowlisted, 8 exempted, 0 failures. The tests that touch the tuple derive from it rather than hardcoding a length. scripts/ops/status_check.sh keeps its own list and globs ict-* only. No liveness surface starts asserting on ssh.service.

NOT GUARDED, SAID OUT LOUD: sshd ships no deploy/*.service of ours, so check_diag_unit_allowlist.py never scans this entry -- the same blind spot caddy.service carries, and the comment says so at the line.

PRIVACY, STATED AND ACCEPTED: sshd journal lines carry source IPs and usernames and everything holding the diag bearer can now read them. That cost was put to the operator and accepted (row E27). It adds no WRITE route and returns no secrets, so the closed diag-token rotation decision in docs/reference/diag-access.md is not reopened by it.

VALIDATION: tests/test_web_api_diag.py + tests/test_diag_timers.py + tests/test_check_diag_unit_allowlist.py -> 52 passed; check_diag_unit_allowlist / check_skills_index / check_canonical_doc_coherence / check_collapsed_states / check_document_index all pass. check_unwired_artifacts fails, and it fails identically on unmodified `main` (baseline checked) -- pre-existing, not this diff.

NOT DONE AT MERGE. The row closes only when the probe that 400s today returns 200 with journal lines against the RUNNING web-api, i.e. after the deploy. Until then E27 is landed_unproven.
